questions.title: malloc Return Type
questions.description: What does malloc(size_t n) return on success?
questions.Option1: A void * pointer to n bytes of uninitialized memory
questions.Option2: A void * pointer to n bytes of zero-initialized memory
questions.Option4: An integer representing the allocated size

questions.title: calloc vs malloc Difference
questions.description: How does calloc differ from malloc?
questions.Option1: calloc takes a count and a size, and zero-initializes the allocated memory
questions.Option2: calloc allocates memory only on the stack
questions.Option3: calloc is faster but does not actually allocate memory
questions.Option4: There is no difference; they are aliases for the same function

questions.title: realloc Purpose
questions.description: What is the purpose of realloc(ptr, new_size)?
questions.Option1: Resize a previously allocated block, possibly moving it to a new location
questions.Option3: Allocate a brand new block without regard to ptr
questions.Option4: Copy bytes from one block to another

questions.title: free Function Behavior
questions.description: What does free(ptr) do when ptr was returned by a successful malloc?
questions.Option1: Deallocates the memory block pointed to by ptr so it can be reused
questions.Option3: Fills the memory block with zeros
questions.Option4: Returns the number of bytes freed

questions.title: Memory Leak Definition
questions.description: What is a memory leak in C?
questions.Option1: Allocated memory that is no longer reachable by the program but has not been freed
questions.Option2: A pointer that is set to NULL after being freed
questions.Option3: An array that is allocated on the stack instead of the heap
questions.Option4: A compiler warning about unused variables

questions.title: Why Dynamic Allocation
questions.description: Why use dynamic memory allocation for large data structures in C?
questions.Option1: It allows array sizes to be determined at runtime and avoids fixed stack-size limits
questions.Option2: Dynamic memory is always faster than stack memory
questions.Option4: Dynamic memory is required to use pointers at all

questions.title: Required Header for malloc
questions.description: Which standard header must be included to use malloc, calloc, realloc, and free?

questions.title: calloc Argument Count
questions.description: How many arguments does calloc take?
questions.Option1: Two: a count of elements and the size of each element
questions.Option2: One: the total number of bytes to allocate
questions.Option3: Three: count, size, and an initial value

questions.title: realloc NULL Behavior
questions.description: What does realloc(NULL, n) do?
questions.Option1: Behaves like malloc(n), allocating a new block of n bytes

questions.title: free NULL Safety
questions.description: What happens if you call free(NULL)?
questions.Option1: It is a safe no-op and does nothing
questions.Option4: It allocates one byte of memory
